subject: Goods and Services Tax
question_html: GST is described as a "destination-based tax". What does this mean in the context of determining tax liability?

options.A: The tax is levied at the place where the goods or services are consumed, rather than the place where they are produced
options.B: The tax is levied at the place where the goods or services are produced, rather than the place where they are consumed
options.C: The tax is levied at the place where the supplier is registered, irrespective of consumption
options.D: The tax is levied equally in both the origin State and the destination State

answer_html:
Correct Answer: A. The tax is levied at the place where the goods or services are consumed, rather than the place where they are produced

GST is a destination-based tax, i.e. the tax is levied at the place where the goods or services are consumed, rather than the place where they are produced. Determining the correct 'place of supply' and 'location of the supplier' is essential to ascertain whether a supply is intra-State (attracting CGST plus SGST/UTGST) or inter-State (attracting IGST).

subject: Goods and Services Tax
question_html: As per section 2(86) of the CGST Act, the term 'place of supply' means:

options.B: The place of supply as referred to in Chapter V of the Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
options.A: The registered place of business of the supplier as recorded in the GST registration certificate
options.C: The location where the invoice for the supply is issued, irrespective of any other factor
options.D: The head office location of the recipient of the supply, in all cases without exception

answer_html:
Correct Answer: B. The place of supply as referred to in Chapter V of the Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017

Section 2(86) of the CGST Act defines 'place of supply' to mean the place of supply as referred to in Chapter V of the IGST Act, 2017 (i.e. sections 10 to 14). In simple words, 'place of supply' is the place where the supply is consumed, and it determines the jurisdiction where the tax revenue should reach.

question_html: As per section 2(3) of the IGST Act, 'continuous journey' means a journey for which a single or more than one ticket or invoice is issued at the same time, and which involves no stopover between any of the legs of the journey. In this context, what does the term 'stopover' mean?

options.C: A place where a passenger can disembark either to transfer to another conveyance or break his journey for a certain period in order to resume it at a later point of time
options.A: A place where the conveyance halts only for refuelling, without any passenger being permitted to disembark
options.B: The final destination point of the journey as mentioned on the last leg of the ticket
options.D: Any intermediate airport or railway station through which the conveyance merely passes without stopping

answer_html:
Correct Answer: C. A place where a passenger can disembark either to transfer to another conveyance or break his journey for a certain period in order to resume it at a later point of time

As per the Explanation to section 2(3) of the IGST Act, 'stopover' means a place where a passenger can disembark either to transfer to another conveyance or break his journey for a certain period in order to resume it at a later point of time. The term 'conveyance' has been defined in section 2(34) of the CGST Act to include a vessel, an aircraft and a vehicle.

subject: Goods and Services Tax
question_html: As per section 2(14) of the IGST Act, where a supply of service is received at a place of business for which registration has been obtained, the 'location of the recipient of services' shall be:

options.A: The location of such registered place of business
options.B: The location of the fixed establishment most directly concerned with receipt of the supply, regardless of whether registration exists
options.C: The usual place of residence of the recipient, irrespective of the place at which the supply is actually received
options.D: The location of the recipient's head office, even if the supply is received at a different registered branch

answer_html:
Correct Answer: A. The location of such registered place of business

As per section 2(14), where a supply is received at a place of business for which registration has been obtained, the location of such place of business is the location of the recipient of services. Only where a supply is received at a fixed establishment elsewhere, or at more than one establishment, or in the absence of such places, do the subsequent limbs of the definition (fixed establishment most directly concerned, or usual place of residence) apply.

subject: Goods and Services Tax
question_html: Section 2(15) of the IGST Act defines the 'location of the supplier of services'. Which of the following statements correctly describes the position with respect to 'location of supplier of goods'?

options.C: The term 'location of supplier of goods' has not been defined in the Act; taking a cue from the definition of place of supply, it is understood to be where the business is ordinarily carried on or where the goods themselves are located
options.A: The term 'location of supplier of goods' is defined identically to 'location of supplier of services' under section 2(15) of the IGST Act
options.B: The location of supplier of goods is always the State mentioned in the GST registration certificate of the supplier, without any exception
options.D: The location of supplier of goods must always be determined with reference to the fixed establishment definition under section 2(7)

answer_html:
Correct Answer: C. The term 'location of supplier of goods' has not been defined in the Act; taking a cue from the definition of place of supply, it is understood to be where the business is ordinarily carried on or where the goods themselves are located

As pointed out in the Study Material, 'location of supplier of goods' is not defined in the law - only the location of supplier of services is defined under section 2(15). Since goods, being tangible, do not pose the same difficulty as intangible services in ascertaining their location, taking a cue from the definition of place of supply, location of supplier of goods is understood to be where business is ordinarily carried on or where the goods themselves are located.

question_html: As per section 2(85) of the CGST Act, 'place of business' includes all of the following EXCEPT:

options.D: A place where an unregistered casual visitor merely inspects the taxable person's goods without any business activity being conducted there
options.A: A place from where the business is ordinarily carried on, including a warehouse, a godown or any other place where a taxable person stores goods, supplies or receives goods or services or both
options.B: A place where a taxable person maintains his books of account
options.C: A place where a taxable person is engaged in business through an agent, by whatever name called

answer_html:
Correct Answer: D. A place where an unregistered casual visitor merely inspects the taxable person's goods without any business activity being conducted there

Section 2(85) of the CGST Act is an inclusive definition of 'place of business', covering: (a) a place from where the business is ordinarily carried on, including a warehouse, godown, etc.; (b) a place where books of account are maintained; and (c) a place where a taxable person is engaged in business through an agent. Mere inspection by a casual visitor with no business activity does not fall within this inclusive definition.

question_html: As per the proviso to section 2(105) of the CGST Act (as amended), a person who organises or arranges, directly or indirectly, supply of specified actionable claims, including a person who owns, operates or manages a digital or electronic platform for such supply, shall be:

options.A: Deemed to be the supplier of such actionable claims, whether such actionable claims are supplied by him or through him, whether or not consideration for the supply is paid or conveyed to him or placed at his disposal in any manner
options.B: Treated only as an intermediary agent, with the actual person supplying the actionable claim remaining solely liable to pay the tax
options.C: Exempt from GST liability on such platform services, as actionable claims other than lottery, betting and gambling are excluded from the definition of goods and services
options.D: Required to obtain a separate registration only if the value of actionable claims arranged through the platform exceeds the composition threshold

answer_html:
Correct Answer: A. Deemed to be the supplier of such actionable claims, whether such actionable claims are supplied by him or through him, whether or not consideration for the supply is paid or conveyed to him or placed at his disposal in any manner

As per the proviso to section 2(105) of the CGST Act, a person who organises or arranges supply of specified actionable claims, including a person who owns, operates or manages a digital/electronic platform for such supply, is deemed to be the supplier of such actionable claims (whether supplied by him or through him, and whether or not consideration is paid or conveyed to him), and all provisions of the Act apply to him as if he is the supplier liable to pay tax.

question_html: As per section 10(1)(a) of the IGST Act, where the supply of goods involves movement of goods, whether by the supplier or the recipient or by any other person, the place of supply of such goods shall be:

options.B: The location of the goods at the time at which the movement of goods terminates for delivery to the recipient
options.A: The location from where the movement of goods commences, i.e. the supplier's place of business
options.C: The location of the transporter's registered office, irrespective of the origin or destination of the goods
options.D: The location at which the invoice for the supply of goods is generated by the supplier

As per section 10(1)(a) of the IGST Act, in case of a supply involving movement of goods, the place of supply is the location of the goods at the time when the movement of goods terminates (ends) for delivery to the recipient. This provision does not link itself to transfer of property in goods but to the actual movement of the goods.

subject: Goods and Services Tax
question_html: As per section 10(1)(e) of the IGST Act, where the goods are supplied on board a conveyance, including a vessel, an aircraft, a train or a motor vehicle, the place of supply shall be:

options.C: The location at which such goods are taken on board

answer_html:

subject: Goods and Services Tax
question_html: Kanhaiya boards the Mumbai-Bhopal train at Mumbai. He sells goods taken on board by him (at Mumbai) in the train, at Nashik during the journey. What is the place of supply of these goods?

options.D: Mumbai, being the location at which the goods are taken on board, and not Nashik where they have been sold
options.A: Nashik, being the location at which the goods were actually sold to the passengers during the journey
options.B: Bhopal, being the final scheduled destination point of the train for that journey
options.C: Mumbai and Nashik in equal proportion, since the sale transaction spans the journey between these two points

answer_html:
Correct Answer: D. Mumbai, being the location at which the goods are taken on board, and not Nashik where they have been sold

As per section 10(1)(e), the place of supply of goods supplied on board a conveyance is the location at which the goods are taken on board, irrespective of where they are actually sold during the journey. Here, since the goods were taken on board at Mumbai, the place of supply is Mumbai and not Nashik.

question_html: As per section 10(2) of the IGST Act, where the place of supply of goods cannot be determined in terms of the specific rules under section 10(1), how shall the place of supply be determined?

options.A: In such manner as may be prescribed by the Government
options.B: The place of supply shall default automatically to the location of the supplier's principal place of business in every such case
options.C: The place of supply shall default automatically to the location of the recipient's principal place of business in every such case
options.D: Such supplies shall be treated as exempt from GST until the place of supply is subsequently determined by a court of law

answer_html:
Correct Answer: A. In such manner as may be prescribed by the Government

As per section 10(2) of the IGST Act, where the place of supply of goods cannot be determined in terms of the situations specifically covered under section 10(1), the place of supply shall be determined in such manner as may be prescribed by the Government - this is a residual/catch-all provision for cases not otherwise covered.

question_html: As per section 12(1) of the IGST Act, the provisions of section 12 apply to determine the place of supply of services in which of the following circumstances?

options.B: Where the location of supplier of services and the location of the recipient of services are both in India
options.A: Where either the location of supplier of services or the location of the recipient of services is outside India
options.C: Where the location of supplier of services alone is in India, irrespective of the location of the recipient
options.D: Where the recipient of services alone is registered under GST, irrespective of the location of either party

answer_html:
Correct Answer: B. Where the location of supplier of services and the location of the recipient of services are both in India

As per section 12(1) of the IGST Act, the provisions of section 12 apply to determine the place of supply of services where the location of supplier of services and the location of the recipient of services are both in India. Where either party is located outside India, place of supply is instead determined under section 13 (covered at the Final level).

question_html: As per the general rule under section 12(2)(a) of the IGST Act, the place of supply of services (not covered by the specific rules in sub-sections (3) to (14)) made to a registered person shall be:

options.C: The location of such registered person
options.A: The location of the supplier of services, since the supplier possesses the GSTIN details of the recipient
options.B: The location where the contract for supply of services was executed by both parties
options.D: The location of the recipient's bank branch through which payment for the service was made

As per section 12(2)(a) of the IGST Act, for services not covered by the specific rules under sub-sections (3) to (14), the place of supply made to a registered person is the location of such person. Since the supplier has the GSTIN of the recipient, the location of such GSTIN can be used as the place of supply.

question_html: As per the general rule under section 12(2)(b) of the IGST Act, for services (not covered by sub-sections (3) to (14)) supplied to a person other than a registered person, the place of supply shall be:

question_html: Which of the following categories of services is NOT covered under section 12(3) of the IGST Act (services in relation to immovable property/lodging accommodation)?

options.A: Services by way of transportation of goods, including by mail or courier
options.B: Services provided directly in relation to an immovable property, including those by architects, interior decorators, surveyors and engineers
options.C: Services provided by way of lodging accommodation by a hotel, inn, guest house, home stay, club, campsite, house boat or vessel
options.D: Services provided by way of accommodation in an immovable property for organising a marriage, reception or business function

Correct Answer: A. Services by way of transportation of goods, including by mail or courier

Section 12(3) covers services directly in relation to immovable property (architects, interior decorators, etc.), lodging accommodation by hotels/guest houses/house boats/vessels, and accommodation for organising marriages/receptions/business functions, along with ancillary services. Transportation of goods (including by courier) is instead covered under section 12(8) of the IGST Act.

question_html: As per the proviso to section 12(3) of the IGST Act, if the immovable property, boat or vessel is located or intended to be located outside India, the place of supply of the related service shall be:

options.B: The location of the recipient of the service
options.A: The location of the supplier of the service, regardless of where the recipient is located

question_html: Manthan, a consulting engineer based in Chennai, renders professional services in respect of an immovable property of Kanishk (based in Coimbatore) located in Singapore. Both Manthan and Kanishk are located in India. What is the place of supply?

options.C: Coimbatore, being the location of the recipient, since the immovable property is located outside India, and not the actual location of the property (Singapore)
options.A: Singapore, being the actual location of the immovable property, irrespective of where the supplier and recipient are located
options.B: Chennai, being the location of the supplier, since the immovable property is located outside the taxable territory
options.D: The place of supply cannot be determined under section 12, and section 13 (import/export provisions) must instead be applied since the property is abroad

answer_html:
Correct Answer: C. Coimbatore, being the location of the recipient, since the immovable property is located outside India, and not the actual location of the property (Singapore)

As per the proviso to section 12(3), since the immovable property is located outside India (Singapore) while both the supplier and recipient are located in India, the place of supply is the location of the recipient of services, i.e. Coimbatore, and not the place where the immovable property is located. This should not be confused with cases where either the supplier or recipient itself is located outside India (which fall under section 13).

question_html: Which of the following statements correctly describes the applicability of section 12(3) of the IGST Act to a property that is yet to be constructed or developed?

options.D: Section 12(3) applies equally to property already constructed/developed as well as property yet to be constructed/developed - for example, an architect's services for drawing the plan of a building yet to be constructed are covered, with the place of supply being where the property is intended to be located

options.B: Services relating to a property yet to be constructed are entirely outside the scope of GST until the property comes into existence
options.C: The place of supply for services relating to a yet-to-be-constructed property is always the location of the supplier of the service, regardless of the intended site

answer_html:
Correct Answer: D. Section 12(3) applies equally to property already constructed/developed as well as property yet to be constructed/developed - for example, an architect's services for drawing the plan of a building yet to be constructed are covered, with the place of supply being where the property is intended to be located

question_html: As per the Explanation to section 12(3) of the IGST Act, where the immovable property or boat or vessel is located in more than one State or Union territory, the supply of services shall be treated as made:

options.A: In each of the respective States or Union territories, in proportion to the value for services separately collected or determined in terms of the contract or agreement entered into in this regard, or, in the absence of such contract or agreement, on such other basis as may be prescribed
options.B: Only in the State or Union territory where the largest proportion of the immovable property is physically located
options.C: Only in the State or Union territory where the supplier of the service is registered under GST
options.D: Equally in each such State or Union territory, irrespective of the actual value of services attributable to each location

answer_html:
Correct Answer: A. In each of the respective States or Union territories, in proportion to the value for services separately collected or determined in terms of the contract or agreement entered into in this regard, or, in the absence of such contract or agreement, on such other basis as may be prescribed

As per the Explanation to section 12(3), where the immovable property or boat or vessel is located in more than one State/Union territory, the supply is deemed to be made in each of the respective States/Union territories, in proportion to the value for services separately collected/determined under the contract, or on such other basis as may be prescribed (under rule 4 of the IGST Rules in the absence of a contract).

question_html: Suvarna Hotels charges a consolidated sum of Rs. 45,000 for a guest's stay in its two establishments in Lucknow and Varanasi, where the stay in Lucknow is for 3 nights and in Varanasi for 2 nights, with no separate city-wise break-up specified in the contract. As per rule 4 of the IGST Rules, on what basis is the value of the lodging accommodation service apportioned between the two States?

options.B: In the ratio of the number of nights stayed in each such property (here, in the ratio 3:2 between Lucknow and Varanasi)
options.A: In the ratio of the floor area of each hotel property, regardless of the number of nights stayed at each location
options.C: Equally between the two States, since a single consolidated amount was charged without any State-wise break-up
options.D: In the ratio of the room tariff applicable in each State as separately notified by the respective State Governments

answer_html:
Correct Answer: B. In the ratio of the number of nights stayed in each such property (here, in the ratio 3:2 between Lucknow and Varanasi)

As per rule 4 of the IGST Rules, for lodging accommodation by a hotel, inn, guest house etc. and its ancillary services, the factor determining the proportionate value of service in each State/Union territory is the number of nights stayed in such property. Here, the consolidated amount would be apportioned in the ratio 3:2 (Lucknow:Varanasi), i.e. Rs. 27,000 for Lucknow and Rs. 18,000 for Varanasi.

question_html: Under rule 4 of the IGST Rules, what factor determines the State-wise apportionment of value for (i) other services in relation to immovable property (such as construction services on land spanning multiple States) and (ii) lodging accommodation by a house boat or vessel traversing multiple States?

question_html: Where a vendor arranges hoardings/billboards at a specific location (owning or renting the structure himself) and merely displays the advertising company's advertisement, without any sale of space or grant of rights to use the hoarding to the advertising company, the place of supply of the vendor's service is governed by:

options.A: Section 12(2) of the IGST Act (the general rule), since the service is purely in the nature of an advertisement service and does not amount to sale of advertising space or grant of rights to use immovable property, and so is not covered under section 12(3)(a)

options.D: Section 10(1)(e) of the IGST Act, treating the advertisement display as if it were goods supplied on board a conveyance

answer_html:
Correct Answer: A. Section 12(2) of the IGST Act (the general rule), since the service is purely in the nature of an advertisement service and does not amount to sale of advertising space or grant of rights to use immovable property, and so is not covered under section 12(3)(a)

Such services are purely advertisement services, with the place of supply determined under the general rule in section 12(2).

question_html: As per Explanation 1 to section 8 of the IGST Act, establishments of the same entity shall be considered establishments of 'distinct persons' where a person has:

options.C: An establishment in a State/Union territory and any other establishment outside that State/Union territory, or an establishment in a State/Union territory and any other establishment registered within that same State/Union territory
options.A: Two or more establishments in the same State that are not separately registered, regardless of how business is conducted through them
options.B: A single establishment which supplies goods to unregistered persons only, without any other establishment anywhere else
options.D: An establishment that deals exclusively in goods exempted under Schedule III to the CGST Act

answer_html:
Correct Answer: C. An establishment in a State/Union territory and any other establishment outside that State/Union territory, or an establishment in a State/Union territory and any other establishment registered within that same State/Union territory

As per Explanation 1 to section 8 of the IGST Act, establishments of the same entity are treated as establishments of distinct persons where a person has: (a) an establishment in a State/UT and any other establishment outside that State/UT; or (b) an establishment in a State/UT and any other establishment registered within that same State/UT. A person carrying on business through a branch, agency or representational office in any territory is treated as having an establishment in that territory (Explanation 2).

question_html: As per the provisos to section 8(1) and section 8(2) of the IGST Act, which of the following supplies is NOT treated as an intra-State supply even when the location of supplier and place of supply fall within the same State/Union territory?

options.D: Supply of goods or services to or by a Special Economic Zone (SEZ) unit or SEZ developer

answer_html:
Correct Answer: D. Supply of goods or services to or by a Special Economic Zone (SEZ) unit or SEZ developer

Such supplies are instead treated as inter-State supplies.

question_html: As per section 9 of the IGST Act, where the location of the supplier or the place of supply is in the territorial waters, such location/place of supply shall, for the purposes of the Act, be deemed to be:

options.A: In the coastal State or Union territory where the nearest point of the appropriate baseline is located
options.B: In the Union territory of Lakshadweep, irrespective of the actual location within the territorial waters
options.C: Outside the scope of GST altogether, since territorial waters do not belong to any State or Union territory
options.D: In whichever coastal State the supplier chooses to declare at the time of registration, regardless of the actual location

answer_html:
Correct Answer: A. In the coastal State or Union territory where the nearest point of the appropriate baseline is located

As per section 9 of the IGST Act, notwithstanding anything else contained in the Act, where the location of the supplier or the place of supply is in the territorial waters, it is deemed to be in the coastal State or Union territory where the nearest point of the appropriate baseline is located. This legal fiction ensures every supply is linked to a particular State/UT, since territorial waters do not naturally belong to any State or Union territory.

question_html: Coral Marine Fuels, based in Kochi, Kerala, supplies bunker fuel to a vessel of Trident Shipping Ltd. (registered in Karnataka). The vessel is located at a distance of 8 nautical miles from the nearest point of the baseline of the coastal State of Karnataka and 4 nautical miles from the nearest point of the baseline of the coastal State of Kerala. What is the place of supply?

options.B: Kerala, being the coastal State whose baseline's nearest point is closer to the vessel's location (4 nautical miles, as against 8 nautical miles for Karnataka)
options.A: Karnataka, being the State in which the recipient, Trident Shipping Ltd., is registered under GST
options.C: Kochi, being the location of the supplier's registered place of business, irrespective of the vessel's actual location
options.D: The place of supply cannot be determined since the vessel is located in the territorial waters and not within any State

answer_html:
Correct Answer: B. Kerala, being the coastal State whose baseline's nearest point is closer to the vessel's location (4 nautical miles, as against 8 nautical miles for Karnataka)

As per section 9 of the IGST Act, where the place of supply is in the territorial waters, it is deemed to be in the coastal State whose nearest point of the appropriate baseline is located closest to that place. Since the vessel is 4 nautical miles from Kerala's baseline (closer than the 8 nautical miles from Karnataka's baseline), the place of supply is Kerala.
